rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly with no reported problems, so this round shifts the table toward stronger obfuscation while respecting the hot floating-point loop in flops-3 (a 269-line FP benchmark with only 613 bytes of text). SUB is kept as the dominant cheap transform: near-zero runtime/size cost, high diversity for arithmetic-heavy code. BCF is raised to the strongest heavyweight pass but its RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights stay moderate (~0.45-0.5) so the selector applies it selectively rather than to every function — bogus control flow on a tight FP loop is the biggest overhead risk. FLA remains a secondary flattener with slightly elevated CorrectnessRisk due to PHI-heavy FP regions. SPLIT is a low-cost enabler that improves the effectiveness of FLA/BCF by creating more basic blocks, so it stays active with modest weights. IBR and ICALL are boosted moderately to inter-block and indirect-call obfuscate dispatch points, with ICALL's CorrectnessRisk capped at 0.2 given pointer-heavy FP code. IGV is included at balanced weights with the highest CorrectnessRisk (0.25) since global-variable encoding on FP constants can pertort numeric behavior; the selector should apply it only where safe. Overall the table biases toward SUB+BCF+IBR for resistance, relying on the previous round's verified correctness to justify the increased aggressiveness.
